transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood CSM), Michael Park (CTO, FlintScale), Sofia Ruiz (Head of ML), Devon Lee (Infra), Lina Osei (Finance)

Summary: quick QBR-style checkin covering usage patterns, upcoming seasonal capacity, cost tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated, security handoff items for pilot, and next-step stress test. FlintScale is ramping a new personalization feature in Q3 and wants predictable latency under 300ms p95.

Topics: usage trends, capacity sizing, cost breakdown, VPC/private deployment considerations, SOC2/audit artifacts, pilot timeline, action items

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll go about 45 minutes or so, wanted to do a quick health and capacity handoff ahead of your q3 ramp — michael do you want to kick off with the main goals?
[00:12] Michael Park: yeah thanks jordan. goal is predictable p95 under 300 ms for personalization calls, throughput about 120 rps at peak, and we need cost visibility — lina is, is looking at the run rate. also security needs the SOC2 artifacts before pilot.
[00:27] Jordan Lee: great, lina can you give us a quick sense of runway?
[00:31] Lina Osei: yeah so right now our month-to-date is about $28k a month on inference, with spikes to 40k during promotions. we're trying to cap q3 spend to a 30% increase so we need to know if dedicated capacity buys us predictability.
[00:48] Aisha Khan: okay quick note on the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff — Dedicated gives headroom and stable latency, but you trade some flexibility on model switching. we can recommend autoscale policies and burst pools if you want the best of both.
[01:05] Sofia Ruiz: curious about quantization — can we get similar accuracy if we move to 4-bit for the heavier reranker? accuracy drop tolerance is like 0.5% absolute.
[01:15] Aisha Khan: in our experience many reranker models compress well with minimal quality loss; we have quantization profiles we can run against your eval set. we'll need a sample prompt set and a few hundred responses to validate.
[01:29] Devon Lee: for VPC peering, our infra is on GCP, and we prefer private deployment with customer-managed keys. is that supported?
[01:36] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC with KMS/HSM integrations — we can hand over the network diagram and KMS guide. we'll also include the SOC2 PDF. LINK: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-2025.pdf (note: internal doc)
[01:52] Michael Park: perfect. on latency, our current internal baseline with hosted endpoints on provider X is 320ms p95, so we'd need to shave ~20%. what tuning levers do you suggest?
[02:04] Aisha Khan: batching, KV cache prefixing, and smaller model variants for short queries. we can recommend batching parameters by looking at your inter-arrival distribution; devon if you can share that we'll run a baseline. also model compilation/kernels matter — we picked up better p95 on A100s with certain token lengths.
[02:25] Devon Lee: i'll export the traffic histogram and send over by thursday.
[02:29] Jordan Lee: thanks. lina on cost — we can show committed capacity pricing vs on-demand. committed helps when you have predictable peak windows.
[02:37] Lina Osei: what's the minimum commit we should expect?
[02:40] Jordan Lee: typically we recommend a 3-month trial with a moderate commit that covers 60-70% of expected peak, plus burst on-demand. i'll include scenarios in the pricing matrix.
[02:52] Sofia Ruiz: also wondered about failover — if Dedicated goes down do we have automated fallback to hosted so the feature doesn't go dark?
[02:58] Aisha Khan: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies. we can do blue-green or canary and automatic fallback to hosted model variants. we should design SLA thresholds and the rollback window.
[03:12] Michael Park: good — security-wise, will you provide audit logs and token-level tracing? our compliance team insists on that.
[03:19] Carlos Mendez: yes, audit logs and per-token tracing are available in Redwood Console, we can export logs to your SIEM via S3 or direct log streaming. we'll share the retention policy and options.
[03:34] Devon Lee: any hidden costs for KV cache warm-up or priming requests?
[03:39] Aisha Khan: there is some initial priming cost but it pays off quickly; caching reduces per-token compute and cuts steady-state cost. we'll model that in the cost scenarios.
[03:49] Michael Park: competitors — we've been talking to BigCloudAI and EdgeServe; cost for BigCloudAI was attractive but they struggle on sustained p95 under load.
[03:58] Jordan Lee: noted. we'll include a simple 3-row comparison.
[04:02] Sofia Ruiz: for the pilot can we run a synthetic replay of 72 hours of production traffic? want to see tail latency.
[04:08] Aisha Khan: absolutely; that's our recommended stress test. SE will craft synthetic workload scripts and coordinate network peering to mimic your VPC egress.
[04:17] Devon Lee: our security lead wants the encryption at rest details — we use CMEK in GCP for other services, will that map?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: yes we can support CMEK via our Private deployment; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with KMS integrations. we'll document both options.
[04:33] Michael Park: timeline — if we finalize commit mid-may can we start pilot late may?
[04:38] Jordan Lee: yes pilot kickoff late May is achievable. we'll need the traffic data, contact for network peering, and approval from finance on the pilot budget.
[04:47] Lina Osei: i'll review the pilot budget but expect a yes pending the pricing matrix.
[04:52] Carlos Mendez: to recap next steps: jordan will share pricing scenarios and committed capacity options; aisha will send stress test plan; devon will share traffic histogram and peering contact; carlos will share security doc links and intro to security lead.
[05:08] Jordan Lee: perfect. any other questions?
[05:12] Sofia Ruiz: small ask — can we get an initial eval run on our reranker at 4-bit to verify quality?
[05:18] Aisha Khan: yes send the eval set and we'll run quantization profiles, expect initial results in 3 business days after we receive sample.
[05:28] Michael Park: thanks everyone this was helpful.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. meeting end.

End of transcript.
